messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and outgoing packet loss observed from prod-eu2 private subnets. NAT gateway nat-gw-0a1b2c3d (AZ-b) health checks failing, paging oncall.networking.

sandeep: on pager. seeing spike in 504s and tcp retransmits in prometheus for egress. starting live diagnostics.

maria: tcpdump shows SYNs to 8.8.8.8 not completing, lots of RSTs and retransmits. packet drop ~30% last 10m on az-b subnets.

jon: did anyone touch route tables or NAT infra recently? tagging @lina and @deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline #5123 (feature/egress-optimizations) completed 3h ago, no changes detected in prod-eu2.

lina: no manual terraform applies from platform in last 2h. there was a metadata tag job earlier for secondary-route tags but that was in AZ-a.

sandeep: checking AWS: nat-gw shows as available but associated ENI eni-azb-7f9 has high NetworkPacketsDropped. route table rtb-0abc1234 shows expected 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-0a1b2c3d. propagation shows one assoc as STALE. opening support case.

aws-support: Case 123456789 created. We observe a partial network impairment impacting ENIs in AZ-b for the tenant account. Investigation ongoing. Estimated remediation 30-60m. Recommend failing over traffic.

maria: conntrack on a private instance shows table nearing capacity, many CLOSE_WAIT. could be cascading from ENI drops.

jon: since this is managed NAT, local conntrack overflow seems unlikely to fix; prefer moving routes to healthy gateway in AZ-a to restore egress quickly. note: will break in-flight connections (websockets).

lina: preparing emergency route override to point rtb-0abc1234 to eni-4d5e6f7g (nat-gw-4d5e6f7g in AZ-a).

sandeep: applying override (runbook step 3). command: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-4d5e6f7g```

infra-bot: timeline: route override applied at 3791234605.

maria: monitoring: packet drop on affected flows went from ~30% -> ~2% within 2m. websockets show reconnection spikes but most traffic resumes.

jon: good recovery. confirm that DNS unchanged; this is purely route-level mitigation.

aws-support: update: hardware fault on AZ-b network fabric suspected, migration to spare capacity in progress. Recommend leaving failover in place until confirmed healthy.

maria: customer impact estimate: ~1.2k active sessions across 3 enterprise tenants affected, API error rate ~4x for ~15m pre-failover. no persisted data loss; impact = transient connectivity. suggest status page + direct outreach for affected accounts.

ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-9843 created. severity: Sev2. Notifying trust and comms.

lina: drafting status: "Outbound egress impairment in eu-west-2 AZ-b affecting some API calls & websockets. We rerouted traffic to healthy gateway; services are recovering. Monitoring AWS remediation." add ETA and next update window?

jon: add ETA: recovery expected within 1 hour; next update in 15m. LGTM. ping trust.

maria: adding to postmortem notes: suspected root cause = AZ network impairment causing managed NAT ENI packet drops. mitigation = manual route override to healthy AZ NAT. followups = TF drift check, automated cross-AZ failover.

sandeep: aws-support says spare capacity migration may restore ENI health. they asked us to hold failover until they confirm. we'll keep override until then.

lina: handing off to next oncall: @lina -> @andre. summary: rtb-0abc1234 overridden to eni-4d5e6f7g at 3791234605, aws case 123456789 open, traffic normalized.

andre: ack, taking over. I'll monitor nat metrics and ENI drops for 1h. keep incident open until AWS confirms. assign followups: jon -> TF drift, lina -> runbook automation, maria -> customer comms.

maria: status page updated: "Investigating - partial outbound egress issues in eu-west-2. We have rerouted traffic and are monitoring recovery." :information_source: 

infra-bot: reminder scheduled: update incident ticket in 15m.

andre: leaving note: current status RECOVERING. will post next at 3791234800 or on AWS update. last_message_ts 3791234720.

sandeep: quick retrospective thought: mitigation was correct; we should automate health-based cross-AZ routing to eliminate manual override latency. adding to action items.

lina: agreed. will include runbook automation in postmortem. handing over tcpdumps and logs to infra-runbooks.

andre: thanks all. handoff complete. participants logged.
